sum_exceptions.reason: Rounding. ICE's FY2024 annual report (Figure 17) prints the ICE (12,232) and CBP (25,489) averages, each rounded to a whole person; the total, 37,722, comes from the FY2027 budget overview. Average daily populations are not whole counts, so separately rounded parts can miss the rounded total by one.

disagreements.evidence: In FY 2014, ICE conducted 213,179 removals of recent border crossers.
disagreements.resolution: Typo in the FY2014 report's prose. The same report's bullet and its Border Patrol + Field Operations table (205,058 + 8,661) give 213,719, which also completes the national total (102,224 + 213,719 = 315,943); the FY2015 report's Figure 6 prints 213,719.

disagreements.evidence: During FY 2024, ERO conducted 113,431 administrative arrests, including 33,243 at-large arrests
disagreements.resolution: The FY2024 report's summary page says 33,243; its at-large section and Figure 8 say 33,242, and Figure 8's three categories sum to 33,242. 33,242 is used.

notes.title: FY2003 spans the creation of ICE
notes.text: ICE began operating on March 1, 2003, partway through fiscal year 2003 (Oct 2002–Sep 2003). ICE's FY2003 figure is the first it publishes; the months before March were carried out by the former INS and the Customs Service. Treat FY2003 as a part-year ICE count. (General knowledge — not stated in the snapshot.)

notes.title: Removals only — returns not included
notes.text: ICE states that its removal data include returns starting in FY2007. FY2003–FY2006 are therefore removals only, and FY2007's jump over FY2006 is partly a change in what is counted, not only in enforcement. Do not read the FY2006→FY2007 step as a like-for-like change.

notes.title: “Removals” include returns
notes.text: From FY2007 ICE's removal count includes returns — voluntary returns, voluntary departures and withdrawals under docket control — in addition to removals under an order of removal. ICE's own definition (dashboard glossary, FY2024 annual report) still says so. Compare with DHS or OHSS series that count removals alone and the numbers will differ.

notes.title: Counts are locked on October 5; later closures roll into the next year
notes.text: Since FY2009 ICE locks each year's statistics around October 5 and counts only removals or returns already confirmed. Departures confirmed after that date are counted in the following fiscal year, so a year's figure can include some prior-year departures ('lag'). ICE publishes alternate 'excluding lag' totals for some years (for example FY2013: 363,144); this series always uses ICE's headline, as-locked figure.

notes.title: FY2010 excludes 76,732 CBP expedited removals
notes.text: ICE notes that its FY2010 figure does not include 76,732 expedited-removal cases ICE closed on behalf of CBP (33,900 from a joint CBP/ICE operation in Arizona).

notes.title: From June 1, 2013, un-detained expedited removals and voluntary returns are not ICE removals
notes.text: ICE counts expedited removals and voluntary returns only when ICE took the person into custody (an ICE intake). Voluntary returns recorded on or after June 1, 2013 without an ICE intake are not recorded as ICE removals; those are processed mainly by Border Patrol and published by CBP.

notes.title: Title 42 expulsions are not removals
notes.text: From March 2020 until May 11, 2023, many border crossers were expelled under Title 42 (public-health authority) rather than removed under Title 8. ICE excludes expulsions from its removal count (62,545 in FY2023 alone), which depresses FY2020–FY2023 relative to earlier years.

notes.title: From May 12, 2023, Border Patrol expedited removals flown by ICE Air are included
notes.text: ICE's glossary: as of May 12, 2023, people processed for expedited removal and turned over from Border Patrol to ICE for removal via ICE Air are also counted as ICE removals.

notes.title: FY2021 is read from a chart
notes.text: The FY2021 figure comes from ICE's FY2019–FY2024 removals bar chart in the FY2024 annual report (Figure 23), which labels each bar. ICE's own FY2021 annual-report PDF could not be retrieved. The other five bars in that chart match the figures printed in text elsewhere in ICE's documents.

notes.title: FY2025 comes from ICE's budget submission and is preliminary
notes.text: No ICE annual report or locked statistics file for FY2025 has been published. The figure is ICE's reported result for the measure 'total number of aliens returned and removed' in its FY2027 budget overview (a DHS document). The same table reports FY2024 as 271,484, identical to the annual report. Marked preliminary because ICE has not confirmed it as locked and may restate it.

notes.title: Arresting agency is who first apprehended the person
notes.text: ICE splits its removals, book-ins and detention population by the agency that first apprehended the person. ICE's FY2024 annual report: "The 'ICE' Arresting Agency includes ERO, HSI and other programs. The 'CBP' Arresting Agency includes the following programs: Border Patrol, Inspections, Inspections-Air, Inspections-Land and Inspections-Sea." A CBP row is still an ICE count (ICE removed or detained someone CBP apprehended), not a CBP figure. It is not strictly interior versus border: CBP includes ports of entry, and ICE removals of people ICE arrested are what ICE calls interior removals.

notes.title: Through FY2016 ICE called the split interior and border removals
notes.text: ICE's FY2013–FY2016 reports split removals into interior and border removals rather than by arresting agency. Their definitions: "Interior Removal: An individual removed by ICE who is identified or apprehended in the United States by an ICE officer or agent. This category excludes those apprehended at the immediate border while attempting to unlawfully enter the United States." "Border Removal: An individual removed by ICE who is apprehended by a CBP officer or agent while attempting to illicitly enter the United States at or between the ports of entry." They are stored as arresting agency ICE and CBP. FY2016 appears under both labels with identical figures (65,332 and 174,923 in the FY2016 report; the same as removals by arresting agency in the FY2018 report).

notes.title: FY2008–FY2012 interior and border removals are read from a chart
notes.text: These come from the bar labels of Figure 6 (FY 2008-2015 ICE Removals, Interior and Border) in ICE's FY2015 report, the only saved ICE document that covers these years. The text layer prints the labels out of order, so each was assigned to its year and segment from the rendered page. Each year's two labels add up to ICE's total removals for that year.

notes.title: Criminality is what ICE's systems recorded at the time
notes.text: ICE's definitions (FY2019 report): "Convicted Criminal: Immigration Violators with a criminal conviction entered into ICE systems of record at the time of the enforcement action; Pending Criminal Charges: Immigration Violators with pending criminal charges entered into ICE system of record at the time of the enforcement action; Other Immigration Violators: Immigration Violators without any known criminal convictions, or pending charges entered into ICE system of record at the time of the enforcement action." Convictions include immigration crimes: "Immigration crimes include 'illegal entry,' 'illegal reentry,' 'false claim to U.S. citizenship,' and 'alien smuggling.'" (FY2018 report). A person with both a conviction and pending charges is counted as convicted (FY2017 report). "Other immigration violator" means no record in ICE's systems at that moment; it is not a finding about the person's history.

notes.title: FY2013–FY2015: convicted or not, no pending-charges category
notes.text: ICE's FY2013–FY2015 reports split removals only into convicted criminals and removals without a criminal conviction; pending charges are not a separate category, so those years have two categories, not three (none is set to zero). ICE's definition then: "ICE defines criminality via a recorded criminal conviction obtained by ICE officers and agents from certified criminal history repositories." (FY2014 report); "Criminality is determined by the existence of a criminal conviction within the Crime Entry Screen for an individual." (FY2015 report). ICE prints earlier convicted counts (FY2007, FY2008) but warns that its crime entry screen did not exist before 2011, so they are not used.

notes.title: FY2016's three categories come from the FY2018 report
notes.text: ICE's own FY2016 report split removals two ways: 138,669 convicted and 101,586 without a conviction. Its FY2018 report splits FY2016 three ways (138,669 convicted, 12,163 pending charges, 89,423 other immigration violators). The two agree: 12,163 + 89,423 = 101,586. The three-way split is used.

notes.title: FY2025: convicted and pending charges combined, no split
notes.text: The only FY2025 criminality figures are two performance measures in ICE's FY2027 budget overview (a DHS document): removals and arrests of people "with criminal convictions or pending criminal charges". They are not split between the two, and there is no figure for other immigration violators. The budget's definition: "An alien's status as a convicted criminal or pending criminal is determined at the time of booking into custody, based on their criminal history record in the Enforcement Integrated Database." For FY2024 the same measures (88,763 removals, 81,312 arrests) equal the annual report's convicted plus pending charges. Preliminary, like every FY2025 figure.

notes.title: ERO administrative arrests
notes.text: "An administrative arrest is the arrest of an alien for a civil violation of U.S. immigration laws, which is subsequently adjudicated by an immigration judge or through other administrative processes." "ERO administrative arrests include all ERO programs. All statistics are attributed to the current program of the processing officer of an enforcement action." (FY2018 report). These are ICE ERO arrests only; Border Patrol apprehensions are not included.

notes.title: At-large arrests are a subset of administrative arrests
notes.text: "An ERO at-large arrest is conducted in the community, as opposed to a custodial setting such as a prison or jail." "ERO administrative arrests reported as 'at-large' include records from all ERO Programs with Arrest Methods of Located, Non-Custodial Arrest, or Probation and Parole." (FY2018 report). Every at-large arrest is also counted in administrative arrests.

notes.title: Detainers issued
notes.text: "A detainer is a request to the receiving law enforcement agency to both notify DHS as early as practicable before a removable alien is released from criminal custody, and to maintain custody of the alien for a period not to exceed 48 hours beyond the time the alien would otherwise have been released to allow DHS to assume custody for removal purposes." (FY2018 report). This counts detainers ICE issued, not ones honored, and not people (one person can have more than one).

notes.title: Initial book-ins
notes.text: "An initial book-in is the first book-in to an ICE detention facility to begin a new detention stay. This population includes aliens initially apprehended by CBP who are transferred to ICE for detention and removal." (FY2018 report). Transfers between facilities are not counted.

notes.title: Average daily population in ICE detention
notes.text: "ERO's Average Daily Population (ADP) measures the number of individuals in ICE custody on an average day during the fiscal year." (FY2019 report). "ICE Detention data exclude ORR transfers/facilities, as well as U.S. Marshals Service Prisoners." (FY2024 report). An average, not a count of people detained during the year.

notes.title: Some detention totals come from ICE's budget submission
notes.text: ICE's FY2024 annual report charts the average daily population by arresting agency but prints no total. The FY2021, FY2022, FY2024 and FY2025 totals come from the performance measure 'Average daily population of aliens maintained in detention facilities' in ICE's FY2027 budget overview (a DHS document); FY2023 also appears in ICE's FY2023 annual-report release. FY2021–FY2023 equal the sum of the two agencies exactly; FY2024's parts sum to 37,721 against 37,722 (rounding). FY2025 is preliminary.

notes.title: Some FY2016 figures are read from chart images
notes.text: ICE's FY2018 report is the only saved ICE document with FY2016 administrative arrests, at-large arrests by criminality, initial book-ins by arresting agency, and the FY2016 other-immigration-violator removals. Its charts are images with no text layer, so those numbers are read from snapshots of the rendered pages (in pipeline/raw/ice). Where the report's prose prints a related number, it agrees: 143,470 − 33,366 = 110,104 arrests; 105,736 − 10,985 = 94,751 convicted arrests; 12,163 + 89,423 = 101,586 removals without a conviction.

notes.title: No printed arrest total for FY2021–FY2022
notes.text: ICE's FY2024 annual report charts FY2021 and FY2022 administrative arrests by criminality (Figure 6) but prints no total, and ICE's FY2021–FY2022 annual reports could not be retrieved. The three categories are complete, so they add up to the year's arrests, but no ICE total is stored to check them against.
